title: On-Prem Packaging: Binary Compatibility, SBOM, and License Audit Playbook
author: Priya Nandakumar
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the required checks, automation, and escalation steps for on-prem packaging artifacts shipped to customers. It covers binary compatibility verification, Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) generation and verification, license scanning and audit gating, and runtime compatibility validation for Redwood Private deployments.

Scope:
- Applies to all on-prem packages, container images, and single-file runtime artifacts created by rbuild and the redwood-package-service intended for customer air-gapped or VPC-private installs.
- Excludes ephemeral test images used only in CI test clusters (those are covered by the CI test plan).

Goal and exit criteria:
- Every released artifact must have a reproducible build trace, SBOM, and cryptographic signature.
- No high- or critical-license violations allowed. Medium-risk license findings must have documented business approval.
- Runtime compatibility tests must pass on the declared target host matrix before release.

Definitions:
- Artifact: Any binary, container image, or package (RPM/DEB/tar.gz) intended for customer deployment.
- Build trace: Deterministic list of inputs (git hash, build script, base image digest, toolchain versions) to reproduce an artifact.
- SBOM: Software Bill of Materials (SPDX v2.2 or CycloneDX 1.4).

Pre-flight checks (CI/CD gate - enforced):
1) Reproducible inputs captured: git commit, build container digest, rbuild flags.
2) SBOM generated via syft: syft <artifact> -o spdx-json > artifact.spdx.json
3) Cryptographic signing: cosign sign-blob --key $COSIGN_KEY artifact.tar.gz 
4) Checksum verification: sha256sum artifact.tar.gz > artifact.sha256
5) License scan: grype artifact.tar.gz -o json > grype.json; no HIGH/CRITICAL allowed.
6) Vulnerability threshold: no CVE with score >= 9.0 in image layers that are not patched or whitelisted.

Packaging steps (recommended procedure):
1) Create build environment via rbuild with pinned base image digests (do not use :latest tags). Example: rbuild build --commit $GIT_SHA --base-image "gcr.io/redwood/base@sha256:..." --output /artifacts/myservice-1.2.3.tar.gz
2) Generate SBOM: syft /artifacts/myservice-1.2.3.tar.gz -o spdx-json > /artifacts/myservice.sbom.spdx.json
3) Run license scan: grype /artifacts/myservice-1.2.3.tar.gz -o json > /artifacts/grype.json
4) Sign artifact and SBOM: cosign sign-blob --key $COSIGN_KEY /artifacts/myservice-1.2.3.tar.gz; cosign sign-blob --key $COSIGN_KEY /artifacts/myservice.sbom.spdx.json
5) Publish to staging registry with digest pinning and set immutability tag policy.

SBOM generation and verification:
- Format: Prefer SPDX JSON v2.2 for all on-prem artifacts. CycloneDX allowed if produced by a toolchain requirement.
- Content requirements: component name, version, supplier, checksums (sha256), file-level relationships, and build environment metadata.
- Verification step (post-build):
  a) Verify SBOM checksum matches artifact: sha256sum -c artifact.sha256
  b) Validate SBOM schema: jq -e . < artifact.sbom.spdx.json >/dev/null || exit 1
  c) Cross-check SBOM components against grype findings to ensure no conflicting entries.

License scanning and audit gating:
- Primary tool: grype (config: policies/license-policy.yml).
- Policy: block releases with any HIGH/CRITICAL license issues (GPLv3 with static linkage, AGPL where distribution triggers server-side obligations, or proprietary licenses with incompatible terms).
- Medium license issues: require a documented exception with legal and product sign-off in the release ticket.
- Manual audit: For any package with non-standard licensing, run a manual license review template (see Appendix) and attach to release ticket.

Compatibility matrix and runtime validation:
- Maintain a published compatibility matrix file (compatibility-matrix.yml) with host OS, kernel versions, glibc, container runtimes, and minimum GPU driver versions. Example matrix rows:

  | Component         | Supported OS      | Kernel        | glibc | Container Runtime | Notes |
  | myservice         | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS  | 5.15.x        | 2.35  | containerd 1.6+   | requires userns-remap off |
  | r-deploy-agent    | RHEL 8.9          | 4.18.x        | 2.28  | docker 20.10      | SELinux permissive required |
- Runtime validation suite (run as part of release pipeline against a matrix):
  - smoke-start: start service, check health endpoint /healthz within 60s.
  - kv-cache-load: run a short workload to validate KV cache warmup within 120s.
  - quantization-check: run a deterministic sample inference and validate output checksum against baseline.
  - gpu-driver-probe: verify NVIDIA driver & CUDA version when GPU images included.

Upgrade and rollback considerations (on-prem specific):
- Upgrade artifacts must include a migration plan file migrations/README.md with step-by-step schema and config changes.
- Backwards compatibility policy: minor releases (<major.minor.patch>) must support config v1. If there is a breaking change, mark with MAJOR and require customer opt-in.
- Rollback artifacts: every release pipeline must publish the previous successful artifact and keep it available for 14 days in the staging registry.
- Emergency rollback steps (customer-facing runbook snippet):
  1) Stop new service: systemctl stop redwood-myservice || docker stop myservice || kubectl scale deploy/myservice --replicas=0
  2) Pull previous artifact by digest and restore: r-deploy-agent install --digest sha256:<previous_digest> --keep-config
  3) Run runtime smoke tests and finish with /healthz green.

Automation and CI checks (enforced in reforged CI):
- Build pipeline gates: reproducible trace, SBOM present, signatures, grype policy, and runtime smoke tests.
- Periodic scheduled checks: weekly re-scan of published artifacts for new CVEs and license changes; results create a security ticket if findings exceed thresholds.
- CI failure policy: any gate failure blocks merge to release branch; release engineer triages within 2 business hours.

Escalation and ownership:
- Packaging owner: eng-packaging (primary: @priya.nandakumar@redwood.ai).
- Security reviewer: eng-security (oncall: @elena.kuznetsova@redwood.ai).
- Legal reviewer for license exceptions: legal-team (triage: samir.patel@redwood.ai).
- Customer-facing issues: customer-success and solutions-eng are notified automatically via release ticket watcher.

Audit evidence and compliance artifacts to attach to release ticket:
- artifact.sha256 and artifact.signature (cosign)
- artifact.sbom.spdx.json (SPDX v2.2)
- grype.json (license/vuln report)
- compatibility-matrix.yml entry used for validation
- migration README if applicable

Appendix: sample commands and manifest examples
- Checksum and verification:
  sha256sum myservice-1.2.3.tar.gz > myservice-1.2.3.tar.gz.sha256
  sha256sum -c myservice-1.2.3.tar.gz.sha256

- Cosign signing example:
  export COSIGN_KEY=/keys/cosign.key
  cosign sign-blob --key $COSIGN_KEY myservice-1.2.3.tar.gz --output-signature myservice.sig
  cosign verify-blob --key $COSIGN_PUB myservice-1.2.3.tar.gz --signature myservice.sig

- Minimal packaging manifest (rbuild-manifest.yml):
  name: myservice
  version: 1.2.3
  base_image: gcr.io/redwood/base@sha256:abcdef1234567890
  toolchain:
    go: 1.20.5
    gcc: 11.3
  sbom_format: spdx-json
  sign_with: cosign

- Example SBOM (SPDX fragment):
  {
    "spdxVersion": "SPDX-2.2",
    "dataLicense": "CC0-1.0",
    "SPDXID": "SPDXRef-DOCUMENT",
    "name": "myservice-1.2.3"
  }

FAQ and common failure modes:
- Failure: grype detects GPLv3 statically linked dependency. Action: build a non-static variant or replace dependency; if unavoidable, file legal exception.
- Failure: SBOM missing file-level checksums. Action: update syft invocation to include file metadata and re-run packaging job.
- Failure: cosign verification fails for customer environment. Action: confirm cosign public key distribution and re-sign artifacts with customer-shared key if required.
